scenarios.observed: On both an Android emulator (API 35, Chrome Custom Tabs) and an iOS simulator (ASWebAuthenticationSession, ephemeral), the release-variant app signs in with authorization code + PKCE in the system browser against the local Keycloak and API with synthetic users. Tokens live only in the OS secure store (session restored after an app restart). After customer-a signs out and the app restarts it is signed out and shows nothing of A; the next sign-in shows the provider's login form again (prompt=login; a defect where the previous person was silently signed back in was found and fixed); customer-b signs in and A's name is absent; 'Switch account' also demands a fresh login and cancelling leaves the app signed out with nothing of B. Client unit tests show cached private data is dropped when the subject changes. Scope note: the app has no order screens yet (MB-032), so opening A's previous order link from the app is not exercisable; the server refuses another customer's order (owner-only order views, MB-018/MB-019 backend tests in BACKEND-VERIFY), and MB-033's acceptance re-checks it natively once order screens exist.

Expo shell with environment configuration (HTTPS required outside development), Arabic default and English with direction, system-browser PKCE with strict redirect checking (wrong scheme/path, forged or missing state, provider error and missing code rejected; unit tests), secure token storage that deletes corrupt, incomplete or expired-unrefreshable sessions, account switch and sign-out that clear private data, and a crash boundary. Release variants with the JS bundle embedded launch on the Android emulator and the iOS simulator with no crash, and the native sign-in round trip passes on both (TC-048). These are emulator/simulator builds, not store or signed device builds (MB-034/MB-035).

findings: Native evidence comes from GitHub-hosted emulator/simulator runs at the same source commit; no physical device, store build or signing identity was used.

Defect found and fixed during review: interactive sign-in reused the provider's browser session, so after sign-out or on account switch the previous person was signed back in without a login form; now prompt=login and an ephemeral iOS session (unit test; mutation removing prompt=login fails it).

The development-identifier Android app permits cleartext to localhost/10.0.2.2 only (config plugin, skipped unless extra.environment is development); the iOS simulator Release build is ad-hoc signed so its keychain works. Neither applies to staging/production builds (O08).
TC-048's order-link clause is covered server-side now and natively in MB-033; this is stated in the scenario observation rather than claimed as exercised in the app.
